notes.text: Go take — This was, probably, done in vision, and was to be told to the people, as other visions were: it was parabolically proposed to them, and might have been sufficient to convince the Jews, would they have considered it, as David considered Nathan's parable. A wife of whoredoms and children - Receive and maintain the children she had before.

The blood — The slaughters made by Jehu's hand or by his order, in Jezreel. The house of Jehu - Which had now possessed the throne, through the reigns of Jehoahaz, Jehoash, and Jeroboam; but the usurper, and his successors adhering to the idolatry of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and adding other sins to it, had now provoked God to declare a sudden extirpation of the family: all this came to pass when Shallum conspiring against Zechariah, slew him, 2 Kings xv, 8-10. The kingdom - After one and forty years tottering it fell to utter ruin and hath so continued to this day.

At that day — When my vengeance hath overtaken the house of Jehu. Break - Weaken and by degrees quite break. The bow - All their warlike provision, power and skill. Jezreel - In this valley it is probable the bloodiest battles in the civil wars were fought; the reason whereof might be, because whoever carried the victory in this place, were soon masters of Samaria and Jezreel, and consequently of the kingdom.

Lo-ruhamah — Not pitied. Israel's name had been through many ages Ruhamah, that is, pitied. God had pitied them, and saved them from their enemies. But now Israel should be no more pitied, God would throw them up to the rage of usurpers, and conspirators.

Save them — I will preserve them, that violence do not swallow them up, nor length of captivity wear them out; and this preserved remnant shall return and be planted in their own land, and there kept in safety. By the Lord - Particularly in that extraordinary deliverance of Hezekiah and Jerusalem, from Sennacherib.

Loammi — That is, not my people. Tho' once you were a peculiar people, you are so no more; you are cast off as you deserved. I will not be your God - I will be a God to you, no more than to any of the Heathen nations. This God executed when he gave them up into the hands of Salmaneser, who sent them where none now can find them.

The children of Israel — Not Israel after the flesh, not those very families that are carried captive. In the place - In those places, were a people dwelt who were not his people, there shall be a people of God. The living God - Who is the fountain of life to all his children, and who enables them to offer living sacrifices to the living God.
Captivity — The captives.
Turn us — Restore us to our former tranquillity, and free us from the troubles which we yet groan under.
Revive us — Give us a second reviving in bringing home the rest of our brethren, and in restraining our enemies.

Will hear — Diligently observe. Will speak - What answer God will give to my prayers. Peace - He will give an answer of peace. Saints - Not to all that are called God's people, but only to those who are truly such.

His salvation — That compleat salvation for which all the Israel of God wait; even the redemption by the Messiah; of which not only Christian, but even Jewish writers understand this place; and to which the following passages properly belong. And the psalmist might well say this salvation was nigh, because the seventy weeks determined by Daniel were begun. Glory - The glorious presence of God, and the God of glory himself, even Christ, who is the brightness of his father's glory.

Kissed — That great work of redemption by Christ, shall clearly manifest God's mercy in redeeming his people Israel, and in the conversion of the Gentiles; his truth in fulfilling that great promise of sending his son, his righteousness in punishing sin, on his son, and in conferring righteousness upon guilty and lost creatures; and his peace or reconciliation to sinners, and that peace of conscience which attends upon it.
Truth — Truth among men. Righteousness - And God's justice shall be satisfied: he shall look down upon sinful men with a smiling countenance.

Before him — As his harbinger. He shall fulfil all righteousness, he shall satisfy the righteousness of God, and shall advance righteousness and holiness among men. Set us - Shall cause us to walk in those righteous ways wherein he walketh. David prays for the favour and blessing of God, ver. 1-6. Expresses confidence in him, by praise mingled with prayer, ver. 7-17. A prayer of David.

glossa.text: *Thou hast blessed, O Lord.* ((AUG.)) A psalm on the new blessing, etc., *as far as* of the turning away of iniquity.
*Thou hast forgiven.* ((ID.)) He speaks of things to come as of things past.
*Thou hast mitigated* ((CASS.)) Diapsalma, of the turning away of anger, that is, of punishment.

*Convert us.* He asks what he knew to be still to come. As if: what I have said as past, I pray may be done. ((AUG.)) *Convert us.* I said prophetically things to come, as past; but here he prays for them as truly to come, saying, Convert and turn away, as if he should say, I have said them as though done. And because I see things to come, and because they are not, I pray that they may be done.

*Is it for ever.* He foresees that this punishment will pass away: *For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive. Thou art angry.* ((AUG.)) The anger of God is every punishment which one suffers. As it was said to Adam when he sinned: *Cursed is the earth in thy work, and in labour and in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat thy bread.* Of anger therefore we are mortal and passible, but renewed in Christ. *From generation.* The first generation was mortal, of anger; the other shall be immortal, of mercy: but neither do we merit this mercy by being converted to God through ourselves, for he himself converts us. And thence he subjoins: *God converting,* as if to say: as the quickening is from thee, so also the conversion.

*O God, thou being turned.* ((CASS.)) Not extending, but God converting. First he gives the will of conversion, afterwards he leads to life. Or, O God, thou being turned from anger at the coming of the Son. *Thou wilt quicken us.* So long a time before it is had. And then, *Thy people shall rejoice in thee,* which before shall rejoice wickedly in itself.

*Shew us, O Lord.* ((AUG.)) This the Prophet foretold by praying, etc., *as far as Blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God ((Matth. V))*. ((CASS.)) *Shew.* Or this one asks that Christ be shewn to him spiritually only; he knew indeed that he was to come, but he asks that we may behold him with a pure heart, not with bodily eyes as the unbelievers: for the Jews saw and crucified him. And for the time to come: *Give us thy salvation,* that is, Christ, to be embraced and possessed, that he be not taken away from us; and thus it is read partly of the present, and partly of the future. *Mercy.* ((AUG.)) Christ is called mercy, because he showed us mercy, teaching that whatever of good a man has is from God, and so man is not proud. But cleaving thus and enjoying God, he rejoices in him.

*I will hear what the Lord speaketh in me.* ((CASS.)) Whence he knows, and by whom it is done, and what he himself bestows in coming. *Peace.* ((AUG.)) Christ. Peace toward God and toward the neighbour, and through Christ.
*Near them that fear him.* ((ID.)) Everywhere demons were worshipped, etc., *as far as* immortal in our body now mortal.
*Mercy,* etc. ((ID.)) After he had said, etc., *as far as how truth is sprung out of the earth ((Luc. VIII))*.
*Truth is sprung out of the earth.* ((ID.)) Confession from man, that he may accuse himself, etc., *as far as* the justification of him that confesses is given.

*Justice shall go before him.* ((ID.)) The first justice of man is, etc., *as far as* and visiting he shall set his steps in the way. *Shall walk.* It shall increase, or shall run before, preparing the way for him; and the Lord shall set his steps in the way made ready.

notes.text: So walk in him — In the same faith, love, holiness.
Rooted in him — As the vine. Built - On the sure foundation.

Through philosophy and empty deceit — That is, through the empty deceit of philosophy blended with Christianity. This the apostle condemns,

1. Because it was empty and deceitful, promising happiness, but giving none.

2. Because it was grounded, not on solid reason, but the traditions of men, Zeno, Epicurus, and the rest. And,

3. Because it was so shallow and superficial, not advancing beyond the knowledge of sensible things; no, not beyond the first rudiments of them.

For in him dwelleth — Inhabiteth, continually abideth, all the fulness of the Godhead. Believers are "filled with all the fulness of God," Eph. iii, 19. But in Christ dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead; the most full Godhead; not only divine powers, but divine nature, Colossians i, 19. Bodily - Personally, really, substantially. The very substance of God, if one might so speak, dwells in Christ in the most full sense.

And ye — Who believe. Are filled with him - John i, 16. Christ is filled with God, and ye are filled with Christ. And ye are filled by him. The fulness of Christ overflows his church, Psalm cxxxiii, 3. He is originally full. We are filled by him with wisdom and holiness. Who is the head of all principality and power - Of angels as well as men Not from angels therefore, but from their head, are we to ask whatever we stand in need of.

By whom also ye have been circumcised — Ye have received the spiritual blessings typified of old by circumcision. With a circumcision not performed with hands - By an inward, spiritual operation. In putting off, not a little skin, but the whole body of the sins of the flesh - All the sins of your evil nature. By the circumcision of Christ - By that spiritual circumcision which Christ works in your heart.

Which he wrought in you, when ye were as it were buried with him in baptism — The ancient manner of baptizing by immersion is as manifestly alluded to here, as the other manner of baptizing by sprinkling or pouring of water is, Heb. x, 22. But no stress is laid on the age of the baptized, or the manner of performing it, in one or the other; but only on our being risen with Christ, through the powerful operation of God in the soul; which we cannot but know assuredly, if it really is so: and if we do not experience this, our baptism has not answered the end of its institution. By which ye are also risen with him - From the death of sin to the life of holiness. It does not appear, that in all this St. Paul speaks of justification at all, but of sanctification altogether.

And you who were dead — Doubly dead to God, not only wallowing in trespasses, outward sins, but also in the uncircumcision of your flesh - A beautiful expression for original sin, the inbred corruption of your nature, your uncircumcised heart and affections. Hath he - God the Father. Quickened together with him - Making you partakers of the power of his resurrection. It is evident the apostle thus far speaks, not of justification, but of sanctification only.

Having blotted out — in consequence of his gracious decrees, that Christ should come into the world to save sinners, and that whosoever believeth on him should have everlasting life. The handwriting against us - Where a debt is contracted, it is usually testified by some handwriting; and when the debt is forgiven, the handwriting is destroyed, either by blotting it out, by taking it away, or by tearing it. The apostle expresses in all these three ways, God's destroying the handwriting which was contrary to us, or at enmity with us. This was not properly our sins themselves, (they were the debt,) but their guilt and cry before God.

And having spoiled the principalities and powers — The evil angels, of their usurped dominion. He - God the Father. Exposed them openly - Before all the hosts of hell and heaven. Triumphing over them in or by him - By Christ. Thus the paragraph begins with Christ, goes on with him, and ends with him.

glossa.text: *Rooted.* The lesser ones in the active life. *Above* others *built up in him.* That is, you greater ones who are in contemplation.

*Deceit.* What the false preachers say about the law. *And vain.* Because in this falsehood there is no usefulness, which sometimes is wont to be in false things. *According to the elements.* He touches those who expound idols more shrewdly, saying, Juno is the air, Neptune the sea; therefore, when he had said *according to philosophy and vain,* he adds, *according to the elements of the world:* as if admonishing that not worshippers of images of whatever kind, but also, as it were, teachers and interpreters of the signs, are to be guarded against.

*Corporeally.* Not because God is corporeal, but he has used a transferred word, because in a temple made by hands he dwelt not corporeally but in shadow, that is, by prefiguring signs. *Corporeally,* because in the body of Christ which he took from the Virgin, as in a temple, God dwells, but not so in the saints, because he is the head in which all the senses, reside; as it were touch alone, in those to whom the Spirit is given by measure, of whom it cannot be said: *The Word was made flesh ((Joan. I))*, nor is any of them called the only-begotten of God.

*Buried together with him.* That is, baptized after the likeness of his burial. *Through the faith of the operation.* That is, by believing the works of God. He expounds one of the works of God, which it is especially necessary for those who wish to rise again to believe, namely that God raised up Christ, and that by the example of Christ he will raise them up whence he subjoins: *Who raised up,* etc.

*Blotting out.* Not only to you Gentiles has God granted pardon, but to us Jews also he has remitted the transgressions which are from the law. And this is, *Blotting out.*

*The handwriting.* He means the sin of Adam, which he took away and fixed to the cross, yet not that alone, others as well: because unless he took away this and the others, we should not be freed from death and hell. While the innocent one is slain, sin is crucified. *The decree,* is the sentence adverse in all men, by which it was said: *You shall die the death,* etc.

 *Fastening it.* That it may now cease, since all sacrifices are fulfilled in the offering of the true Lamb.

*Despoiling the principalities and powers.* By taking away Abraham, Isaac and the rest of the just. *He led across,* he led them far from this kingdom to heaven. *Confidently.* That is, with hope of victory. *Triumphing,* that is, vanquishing them upon the cross, which is not in secret, but *openly.* For if anyone looks upon the perfection of the Church, the ancient enemy is plainly seen to be conquered. Or, *he led across the principalities and powers,* that is, he drove them out from the Church. *Triumphing over them in himself.* By his own death. For, one most true sacrifice having been offered for us, whatever of faults there was (whereby the principalities and powers held us fast for the paying of the punishments of life) he extinguished: whence, therefore, the devil received outwardly the power of slaying the Lord's flesh, thence his inner power which held us was slain.

notes.text: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples — The Jewish masters used to give their followers some short form of prayer, as a peculiar badge of their relation to them. This it is probable John the Baptist had done. And in this sense it seems to be that the disciples now asked Jesus, to teach them to pray. Accordingly he here repeats that form, which he had before given them in his sermon on the mount, and likewise enlarges on the same head, though still speaking the same things in substance. And this prayer uttered from the heart, and in its true and full meaning, is indeed the badge of a real Christian: for is not he such whose first and most ardent desire is the glory of God, and the happiness of man by the coming of his kingdom? Who asks for no more of this world than his daily bread, longing meantime for the bread that came down from heaven? And whose only desires for himself are forgiveness of sins, (as he heartily forgives others, ) and sanctification.

When ye pray, say — And what he said to them is undoubtedly said to us also. We are therefore here directed, not only to imitate this in all our prayers, but to use this very form of prayer. Matt. vi, 9.
Forgive us; for we forgive them — Not once, but continually. This does not denote the meritorious cause of our pardon; but the removal of that hindrance which otherwise would render it impossible.
At midnight — The most unseasonable time: but no time is unseasonable with God, either for hearing or answering prayer.
Matt. vii, 7.
How much more shall your heavenly Father — How beautiful is the gradation! A friend: a father: God! Give the Holy Spirit - The best of gifts, and that which includes every good gift.

glossa.text: *And it came to pass.* After the history of the sisters (who signify the two lives) he brings in the Lord as having prayed, and as having instructed the disciples to pray, because both the prayer which he taught contains in itself the mystery of either life, and the perfection of those lives is to be obtained not by our own strength but by prayers. *When he ceased.* For this reason the Saviour is often brought in praying, that he may lead the disciples on to the pursuit of prayer. Whence, the prayer being ended, he is asked by the disciples, that he may teach how they ought to pray.

*Which of you hath a friend.* After he had set forth the form of prayer to those who asked, he lays upon them also instancy and frequency in praying, so that prayer may be offered not only by day but also by night; for he who at midnight asks loaves of his friend, and persists in the intention of asking, is not cheated of his prayer.

*Trouble me not.* He does not take away the hope of obtaining, but the more vehemently kindles the desire of praying, by showing the difficulty of obtaining. *The door is now.* The door which Paul asks to be opened to him for the speaking of the mystery of Christ, and which John saw opened to him, is the understanding of the divine word, which is shut in the time of a famine of the word of God, when understanding is not given. And the children, that is, those who, dealing out evangelical wisdom like bread, preached it through the whole world, are now with the Lord in eternal rest; and yet by praying it is brought about that he who prays receives understanding from the Lord himself, even if there be lacking a man through whom wisdom may be preached. *I cannot rise. ((AMBR.))* No one fears that he may waken a sleeper, whom he knows to be always watching in prayer.

*Yet because of his importunity,* etc. Many are the snares, and heavy is the sleep of the body, because if the mind begins to sleep, it loses the vigour of its own strength. Shake off therefore thy sleep, that thou mayest knock at the door of Christ, that when thou hast entered there may be opened to thee the treasures hidden and in darkness in Christ Jesus.

*Ask, and it shall be given you.* If a man who is a friend rises and gives, compelled not by friendship but by weariness, how much more does God give, who without weariness most bountifully bestows what is asked. Lest therefore the soul, turned back from the vanity of error, waste away any longer in spiritual want, let us ask the banquet of the word, let us seek the friend who may give, let us knock at the door where hidden things are kept. For he gives great hope, who in promising does not deceive. *For every one that asketh receiveth.* There is need of perseverance, that we may obtain. But if it is given to him that asks, and he that seeks finds, and to him that knocks it is opened, then as for him to whom it is not given, and who does not find, and to whom it is not opened, it appears that he has not sought and asked and knocked well.

*Seek, and you shall find.--The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him in truth, and he will do the will of them that fear him ((Psal. XLIV))*. Others, who do not so ask, James rebukes, saying: *You ask and receive not, because you ask amiss ((Jac. IV))*, because you persevere in your sins.

*And which of you, if he ask his father bread, will he give him a stone,* etc. ((BED.)) Mystically. Bread signifies charity, on account of the greater appetite for it and its necessary use, etc., *as far as* let him stretch himself forth to those things which are before.

*How much more.* An open comparison. For if a sinful man, still weighed down with frail flesh, does not refuse to give temporal things to his sons when they ask, much more does the heavenly Father bestow in heaven goods that do not fail upon sons endowed with his fear and his love.

notes.text: I will go down now and see — Not as if there were any thing concerning which God is in doubt; but he is pleased thus to express himself after the manner of men.
Abraham drew near — This expression intimates, A holy concern. A holy confidence; he drew near with an assurance of faith, drew near as a prince, Job xxxi, 37.

Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, who am but dust and ashes — He speaks as one amazed at his own boldness, and the liberty God graciously allowed him, considering God's greatness, he is the Lord; and his own meanness, but dust and ashes. Whenever we draw near to God, it becomes us reverently to acknowledge the vast distance that there is between us and Him. He is the Lord of glory, we are worms of the earth.

Oh let not the Lord be angry — The importunity which believers use in their addresses to God is such, that if they were dealing with a man like themselves, they could not but fear that he would be angry with them. But he with whom we have to do is God and not man, and he is pleased when he is wrestled with. But why then did Abraham leave off asking when he had prevailed so far as to get the place spared if there were but ten righteous in it? Either,

1. Because he owned that it deserved to perish if there were not so many: as the dresser of the vineyard, who consented that the barren tree should be cut down if one year's trial more did not make it fruitful, Luke xiii, 9. Or,

2. Because God restrained his spirit from asking any further. When God hath determined the ruin of a place, he forbids it to be prayed for, Jer. vii, 16.

glossa.text:
« The cry of Sodom and Gomorrha, » etc. ((AUG. Q. in Gen. )) If we take these words as those not of one doubting, but of one angry and threatening, there is no question. For after the manner of men God speaks to men, and his anger is without disturbance, because he is unchangeable. But often in threatening we say thus: Let us see whether I do not do it to thee, and whether I shall not be able to do it to thee; or, let me know, that is, let me try whether I cannot. But disturbance does not fall upon God. It is the custom of human speech, to which God fits himself, that he may suit himself to human weakness.

((GREG. lib. V Moral., cap. 7.)) But sin with a voice is a fault in action. But sin with a cry is a fault with liberty.

« I will go down and see, » etc. ((GREG., Moral., c. 33.)) Let us not believe men's evil deeds before we prove them. And behold, through angels he came down to know their evils, and finding them wrapped in so great a crime , he as it were passed over his patience, and forestalled them with the fire of judgment before the day of judgment: who judges with tranquillity, that the greater crimes may be slowly believed, and, when truly known, more swiftly punished.

((GREG., lib. I Reg., c. 178, tom. I.)) Whither should God go down, that he might know what things had been done? Or what should he not know, who is everywhere? But that he might give to our ignorance an example of discretion, that we ought not to believe grievous evils on hearing them, he says of himself that he goes down to know, of whom it is plain to all that even without going down he would know all things.

((HILAR., lib. IX, de Trin.)) We have God not knowing that which nevertheless he is not ignorant of. For since he knows the sins to be exceeding great, he goes down again that he may see whether they are consummated; and if they are not yet consummated , that he may know: we understand that he does not then know them because he was ignorant before; but that he then knows, because it is the time for acting. Therefore for God not to know is not a diminution of ignorance, but the fulness of time.

« If there be fifty just men, » etc. ((ISID.)) The number fifty, from which he descends down to ten, signifies penance. Whence also the fiftieth psalm is penitential. If therefore they had been converted, they would have been saved. But when God sees the offenders unwilling to be converted to penance, straightway he restrains the heat of immoderate luxury with the fire of hell. He said that up to ten just men Sodom should not perish, because if in any man the name of Christ be found through the keeping of the ten commandments, he shall not perish. For the figure of the number ten signifies also the cross of Christ.

« I will speak to the Lord, » etc. *((GREG. lib. XVIII Moral., c. 33.)) Mystically.* The more the saints look into the inward things of the Godhead, the more do they see themselves to be nothing. Nowhere is Abraham read to have professed himself ashes and dust, save when he deserved to have speech with God. And he said: « I will speak to my Lord, whereas I am dust, » etc. For perhaps he would have believed himself to be something, if he had not felt the true essence which is above him. Whence David also cries out: « Remember, Lord, that I am dust ((Psal. X)), » etc.


*Morally.* Some it lifts up not through the swelling of understanding, but through works of mercy; certain men, while they see themselves [0129B] to abound in earthly things, do not seek the true riches, and love not the eternal kingdom, because they think temporal things sufficient. The fault therefore is not in the understanding, but in the affection. For all things which God founded are good. But he who uses good things ill, acts so that through the gluttony of voracity he dies by that bread whereby he ought to have lived. Lazarus the poor man had come to rest, torments were racking the proud rich man [n: (Luc. XVI)]: yet Abraham had been rich, who held Lazarus in his bosom. Yet he says: « I will speak to my Lord, whereas I am dust and ashes, » etc. How did he value his riches, who accounted himself dust and ashes? Openly we discern in what place he had set himself, who accounted himself dust and ashes even while he spoke with God. With what punishment therefore are they to be struck, who [0129C] make no progress toward the highest things and exalt themselves over the least?

« There be five. » Five cities were burned with showers of fire. For all who have handled the five senses of the body lustfully are to be burned in the fire to come.

« What if there be found, » etc. ((ALC.)) It is not necessary to take this of every place. But of Sodom it could be said, because God knew that there were not even ten there, and therefore it was thus answered to Abraham, to the aggravating of the iniquity of the Sodomites

« Ten. » The number ten designates the cross of Christ, because the letter X, by which ten is expressed, is formed in the figure of a cross.

« He said. » For he knew that there was not even one there besides Lot; this is said to the aggravating of their iniquity, as in Jeremias: « See if you find a man doing justice ((Jer. V)); as if to say: Find but one, and I spare them.

notes.text: The gods — Before kings and princes.
Temple — Where the ark was. He was not permitted to enter into it. Magnified - For thou hast glorified thy word or promise unto me more than any other of thy glorious perfections.
The kings — A prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles. Hear - The gospel preached among then.
The ways — His wonderful counsel and gracious providences.

Perfect — Will finish the great work of my deliverance. Forsake not - Or, do not give over, the work of my salvation, which is thus far advanced, not by any human help, but by thy power and providence. This psalm is, by many of the Jewish doctors, esteemed the most excellent in the whole book. The omniscience of God is here asserted, ver. 1-6. Proved by two arguments; That he is everywhere present, ver. 7-12. And that he made us, ver. 13-16. This may fill us with pleasing admiration of God, ver. 17, 18. With an holy hatred of sin, ver. 19-22. And with an holy satisfaction in our own integrity, ver. 23, 24. To the chief musician, A psalm of David.

glossa.text:
*A psalm to David himself.* ((CASS.)) The captive, who had wept, as though Jerusalem and the temple were rebuilt, and as a fellow-citizen with that part of Jerusalem which was not captive, that is, with the angels, rejoices and praises first the benefits given him. In the person therefore of the Church, which is in the things above in hope, awaiting to be there in reality, he says, *I will confess.*

*I will confess to thee, O Lord.* First, he commends the benefits given him: secondly, he tells how these are spread abroad unto all, there, *Let them confess to thee, O Lord,* etc. *In the sight.* ((AUG.)) In praising I set before myself the angels, to whom I look to be made equal in dignity hereafter, as I am now. But these in the praise of God set before themselves nothing else but himself. *In the sight* therefore *of the angels,* in that purity wherein the angels behold thee, that in thee alone they may rest, I *will sing to thee.*

*For thy mercy.* ((ID.)) *All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth:* There are no other ways by which he came to us, there are no others by which we may come to him: let us render these to God, mercy in succouring, truth in judging. *Above every holy name of thine.* ((CASS.)) Or above thy holy name, when thy worship became known to us.
*In the soul.* And because in the soul a carnal multiplication can take place, he adds, *strength,* as though: I seek nothing else in the soul but strength.

*Let them confess.* ((ID.)) The second part, where it is said *dici*; read *dicit*, "he tells" how these good things are to be spread abroad unto all. As it were, after my example: *Let them confess,* etc. *All the words of thy mouth.* ((AUG.)) Which have now been revealed everywhere, and sent unto all nations, etc., *as far as* and thus, the fleece being dried, *they heard all the words,* etc.

*Great is the glory.* ((ID.)) If they are humble, they love and sing this; for if they exalt themselves, let them fear what follows. *For the Lord is high. He looketh on the low things.* ((CASS.)) Here is not the human condition, where the humble man is despised and the proud man regarded; but the Lord regards the humble.

*The high he knoweth afar off.* ((AUG.)) The proud man does not this, etc., *as far as* mourning this sojourning, whence it is subjoined.

*If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation.* Otherwise he does not quicken, save *in the midst of tribulation,* whence, *Blessed are they that mourn, woe to them that laugh.*

*Upon the wrath.* ((ID.)) This very thing, that they are angry with me, is thy chastisement upon them, that is, thy punishment. For to be angry is to them a punishment, not *noc* only a fault. While therefore thou permittest this, thou stretchest forth the hand of vengeance upon them all.

*Thy right hand.* God has not a right hand or a left, but the right hand of God is called eternal happiness, the left, temporal happiness. Sometimes therefore he does not save his saints in the left hand, but he always saves them in the right.
*He will repay.* ((AUG.)) What I cannot do, etc., *as far as* in whom the princes of the world found no sin, wherefore they should kill him.

notes.text: So walk in him — In the same faith, love, holiness.
Rooted in him — As the vine. Built - On the sure foundation.

Through philosophy and empty deceit — That is, through the empty deceit of philosophy blended with Christianity. This the apostle condemns,

1. Because it was empty and deceitful, promising happiness, but giving none.

2. Because it was grounded, not on solid reason, but the traditions of men, Zeno, Epicurus, and the rest. And,

3. Because it was so shallow and superficial, not advancing beyond the knowledge of sensible things; no, not beyond the first rudiments of them.

For in him dwelleth — Inhabiteth, continually abideth, all the fulness of the Godhead. Believers are "filled with all the fulness of God," Eph. iii, 19. But in Christ dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead; the most full Godhead; not only divine powers, but divine nature, Colossians i, 19. Bodily - Personally, really, substantially. The very substance of God, if one might so speak, dwells in Christ in the most full sense.

And ye — Who believe. Are filled with him - John i, 16. Christ is filled with God, and ye are filled with Christ. And ye are filled by him. The fulness of Christ overflows his church, Psalm cxxxiii, 3. He is originally full. We are filled by him with wisdom and holiness. Who is the head of all principality and power - Of angels as well as men Not from angels therefore, but from their head, are we to ask whatever we stand in need of.

By whom also ye have been circumcised — Ye have received the spiritual blessings typified of old by circumcision. With a circumcision not performed with hands - By an inward, spiritual operation. In putting off, not a little skin, but the whole body of the sins of the flesh - All the sins of your evil nature. By the circumcision of Christ - By that spiritual circumcision which Christ works in your heart.

Which he wrought in you, when ye were as it were buried with him in baptism — The ancient manner of baptizing by immersion is as manifestly alluded to here, as the other manner of baptizing by sprinkling or pouring of water is, Heb. x, 22. But no stress is laid on the age of the baptized, or the manner of performing it, in one or the other; but only on our being risen with Christ, through the powerful operation of God in the soul; which we cannot but know assuredly, if it really is so: and if we do not experience this, our baptism has not answered the end of its institution. By which ye are also risen with him - From the death of sin to the life of holiness. It does not appear, that in all this St. Paul speaks of justification at all, but of sanctification altogether.

And you who were dead — Doubly dead to God, not only wallowing in trespasses, outward sins, but also in the uncircumcision of your flesh - A beautiful expression for original sin, the inbred corruption of your nature, your uncircumcised heart and affections. Hath he - God the Father. Quickened together with him - Making you partakers of the power of his resurrection. It is evident the apostle thus far speaks, not of justification, but of sanctification only.

Having blotted out — in consequence of his gracious decrees, that Christ should come into the world to save sinners, and that whosoever believeth on him should have everlasting life. The handwriting against us - Where a debt is contracted, it is usually testified by some handwriting; and when the debt is forgiven, the handwriting is destroyed, either by blotting it out, by taking it away, or by tearing it. The apostle expresses in all these three ways, God's destroying the handwriting which was contrary to us, or at enmity with us. This was not properly our sins themselves, (they were the debt,) but their guilt and cry before God.

And having spoiled the principalities and powers — The evil angels, of their usurped dominion. He - God the Father. Exposed them openly - Before all the hosts of hell and heaven. Triumphing over them in or by him - By Christ. Thus the paragraph begins with Christ, goes on with him, and ends with him.

glossa.text: *Rooted.* The lesser ones in the active life. *Above* others *built up in him.* That is, you greater ones who are in contemplation.

*Deceit.* What the false preachers say about the law. *And vain.* Because in this falsehood there is no usefulness, which sometimes is wont to be in false things. *According to the elements.* He touches those who expound idols more shrewdly, saying, Juno is the air, Neptune the sea; therefore, when he had said *according to philosophy and vain,* he adds, *according to the elements of the world:* as if admonishing that not worshippers of images of whatever kind, but also, as it were, teachers and interpreters of the signs, are to be guarded against.

*Corporeally.* Not because God is corporeal, but he has used a transferred word, because in a temple made by hands he dwelt not corporeally but in shadow, that is, by prefiguring signs. *Corporeally,* because in the body of Christ which he took from the Virgin, as in a temple, God dwells, but not so in the saints, because he is the head in which all the senses, reside; as it were touch alone, in those to whom the Spirit is given by measure, of whom it cannot be said: *The Word was made flesh ((Joan. I))*, nor is any of them called the only-begotten of God.

*Buried together with him.* That is, baptized after the likeness of his burial. *Through the faith of the operation.* That is, by believing the works of God. He expounds one of the works of God, which it is especially necessary for those who wish to rise again to believe, namely that God raised up Christ, and that by the example of Christ he will raise them up whence he subjoins: *Who raised up,* etc.

*Blotting out.* Not only to you Gentiles has God granted pardon, but to us Jews also he has remitted the transgressions which are from the law. And this is, *Blotting out.*

*The handwriting.* He means the sin of Adam, which he took away and fixed to the cross, yet not that alone, others as well: because unless he took away this and the others, we should not be freed from death and hell. While the innocent one is slain, sin is crucified. *The decree,* is the sentence adverse in all men, by which it was said: *You shall die the death,* etc.

 *Fastening it.* That it may now cease, since all sacrifices are fulfilled in the offering of the true Lamb.

*Despoiling the principalities and powers.* By taking away Abraham, Isaac and the rest of the just. *He led across,* he led them far from this kingdom to heaven. *Confidently.* That is, with hope of victory. *Triumphing,* that is, vanquishing them upon the cross, which is not in secret, but *openly.* For if anyone looks upon the perfection of the Church, the ancient enemy is plainly seen to be conquered. Or, *he led across the principalities and powers,* that is, he drove them out from the Church. *Triumphing over them in himself.* By his own death. For, one most true sacrifice having been offered for us, whatever of faults there was (whereby the principalities and powers held us fast for the paying of the punishments of life) he extinguished: whence, therefore, the devil received outwardly the power of slaying the Lord's flesh, thence his inner power which held us was slain.

notes.text: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples — The Jewish masters used to give their followers some short form of prayer, as a peculiar badge of their relation to them. This it is probable John the Baptist had done. And in this sense it seems to be that the disciples now asked Jesus, to teach them to pray. Accordingly he here repeats that form, which he had before given them in his sermon on the mount, and likewise enlarges on the same head, though still speaking the same things in substance. And this prayer uttered from the heart, and in its true and full meaning, is indeed the badge of a real Christian: for is not he such whose first and most ardent desire is the glory of God, and the happiness of man by the coming of his kingdom? Who asks for no more of this world than his daily bread, longing meantime for the bread that came down from heaven? And whose only desires for himself are forgiveness of sins, (as he heartily forgives others, ) and sanctification.

When ye pray, say — And what he said to them is undoubtedly said to us also. We are therefore here directed, not only to imitate this in all our prayers, but to use this very form of prayer. Matt. vi, 9.
Forgive us; for we forgive them — Not once, but continually. This does not denote the meritorious cause of our pardon; but the removal of that hindrance which otherwise would render it impossible.
At midnight — The most unseasonable time: but no time is unseasonable with God, either for hearing or answering prayer.
Matt. vii, 7.
How much more shall your heavenly Father — How beautiful is the gradation! A friend: a father: God! Give the Holy Spirit - The best of gifts, and that which includes every good gift.

glossa.text: *And it came to pass.* After the history of the sisters (who signify the two lives) he brings in the Lord as having prayed, and as having instructed the disciples to pray, because both the prayer which he taught contains in itself the mystery of either life, and the perfection of those lives is to be obtained not by our own strength but by prayers. *When he ceased.* For this reason the Saviour is often brought in praying, that he may lead the disciples on to the pursuit of prayer. Whence, the prayer being ended, he is asked by the disciples, that he may teach how they ought to pray.

*Which of you hath a friend.* After he had set forth the form of prayer to those who asked, he lays upon them also instancy and frequency in praying, so that prayer may be offered not only by day but also by night; for he who at midnight asks loaves of his friend, and persists in the intention of asking, is not cheated of his prayer.

*Trouble me not.* He does not take away the hope of obtaining, but the more vehemently kindles the desire of praying, by showing the difficulty of obtaining. *The door is now.* The door which Paul asks to be opened to him for the speaking of the mystery of Christ, and which John saw opened to him, is the understanding of the divine word, which is shut in the time of a famine of the word of God, when understanding is not given. And the children, that is, those who, dealing out evangelical wisdom like bread, preached it through the whole world, are now with the Lord in eternal rest; and yet by praying it is brought about that he who prays receives understanding from the Lord himself, even if there be lacking a man through whom wisdom may be preached. *I cannot rise. ((AMBR.))* No one fears that he may waken a sleeper, whom he knows to be always watching in prayer.

*Yet because of his importunity,* etc. Many are the snares, and heavy is the sleep of the body, because if the mind begins to sleep, it loses the vigour of its own strength. Shake off therefore thy sleep, that thou mayest knock at the door of Christ, that when thou hast entered there may be opened to thee the treasures hidden and in darkness in Christ Jesus.

*Ask, and it shall be given you.* If a man who is a friend rises and gives, compelled not by friendship but by weariness, how much more does God give, who without weariness most bountifully bestows what is asked. Lest therefore the soul, turned back from the vanity of error, waste away any longer in spiritual want, let us ask the banquet of the word, let us seek the friend who may give, let us knock at the door where hidden things are kept. For he gives great hope, who in promising does not deceive. *For every one that asketh receiveth.* There is need of perseverance, that we may obtain. But if it is given to him that asks, and he that seeks finds, and to him that knocks it is opened, then as for him to whom it is not given, and who does not find, and to whom it is not opened, it appears that he has not sought and asked and knocked well.

*Seek, and you shall find.--The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him in truth, and he will do the will of them that fear him ((Psal. XLIV))*. Others, who do not so ask, James rebukes, saying: *You ask and receive not, because you ask amiss ((Jac. IV))*, because you persevere in your sins.

*And which of you, if he ask his father bread, will he give him a stone,* etc. ((BED.)) Mystically. Bread signifies charity, on account of the greater appetite for it and its necessary use, etc., *as far as* let him stretch himself forth to those things which are before.

*How much more.* An open comparison. For if a sinful man, still weighed down with frail flesh, does not refuse to give temporal things to his sons when they ask, much more does the heavenly Father bestow in heaven goods that do not fail upon sons endowed with his fear and his love.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Lord, teach us to pray.
Give us this day our daily bread.
Ask, and it will be given; knock, and the door will open.
We come knocking, and we trust the One inside.
Steadfast love and faithfulness have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.
The Lord will speak peace to the people.
Come, lift your empty hands and worship.
Our Father, hallowed be your name. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Imagine knocking on a friend's door at midnight, needing bread, and keeping at it until the bolt slides back — that is what Jesus says prayer is like.
Lord, teach us to pray.
He does not hand us fancy words. He hands us bread: give us this day, forgive us, lead us, deliver us.
Lord, teach us to pray.
Ask, and it is given; seek, and you find; knock, and the door swings wide — for God gives the Spirit to those who ask.
Lord, teach us to pray.
So come to the door this morning with your hunger and your hope. The God where mercy and truth meet is already reaching for the latch.
Lord, teach us to pray. Amen.
